source.context: TCI page, reference 2). The α-thiocarbocation from the Pummerer reaction of an o-aroyl-substituted sulfoxide is trapped by the adjacent keto oxygen; without a dienophile the paper isolates 4-(ethylthio)-6-phenylthieno[2,3-c]furan. Ac₂O/toluene with catalytic p-TsOH are the conditions the abstract gives as best (they suppress the normal acetoxy-sulfide Pummerer product).

problems.verificationNote: The TCI scheme image could not be downloaded (proxy refusal), so the drawn example could not be identified; this is a representative entry taken from the abstract of ref. 2 (PubMed), which names the product 4-(ethylthio)-6-phenylthieno[2,3-c]furan. The sulfoxide precursor, 2-benzoyl-3-[(ethylsulfinyl)methyl]thiophene, was deduced from the product's ring numbering (Ph on C6, next to the thiophene S; SEt on C4) and not read in the paper; the exact conditions for this entry were not read either. Mechanism follows the TCI page (O-acylation of the sulfoxide, elimination to the thionium/α-thiocarbocation, nucleophilic trapping) with the keto oxygen as internal nucleophile, as in the abstract. A chemist should check the substrate regiochemistry and the conditions.

source.context: TCI page, reference 1) (the page prints the volume as 45). First steps of the synthesis: citronellal treated with the ylide from Ph₃P and CBr₄ gives the 1,1-dibromoolefin (98%), and exposure to n-BuLi gives the terminal acetylene (95%). Solvents and temperatures are in the SI and were not read.

problems.verificationNote: The TCI scheme image could not be downloaded (proxy refusal), so the drawn example 1) was not seen; the structures come from the PMC full text of ref. 1 (citronellal → 1,1-dibromoolefin → terminal alkyne), stereochemistry omitted. The say-my-name.net equation and mechanism images could not be downloaded either. Mechanism is the established one (TCI text gives only the two-step summary): Wittig-type addition of Ph₃P=CBr₂ via betaine/oxaphosphetane, then Br/Li exchange, α-elimination to the vinylidene carbene and Fritsch–Buttenberg–Wiechell 1,2-H shift, deprotonation by the second equivalent of BuLi and aqueous workup. A chemist should check the betaine/oxaphosphetane drawings and the carbene (drawn as [C]=C) in step 2; the alternative pathway (HBr elimination to the bromoalkyne, then Br/Li exchange) is also found in textbooks.

source.citation: Named Reactions Explorer, Hantzsch Pyrrole Synthesis (general equation, R¹ = H, R² = H, R³ = Me).
source.context: General equation of the say-my-name.net page (α-chloro ketone R¹CO–CHClR² + ethyl 3-oxoalkanoate R³COCH₂CO₂Et, NH₃ → ethyl 2-R³-4-R¹-5-R²-pyrrole-3-carboxylate) with R¹ = R² = H (chloroacetaldehyde) and R³ = Me (ethyl acetoacetate); R³ = H would make the β-dicarbonyl component an aldehyde (ethyl formylacetate), so the simplest β-keto ester was used. Product: ethyl 2-methyl-1H-pyrrole-3-carboxylate. The intermediates follow the page's mechanism image: enamine from the β-keto ester and NH₃, C-attack of the enamine on the carbonyl of the chloro carbonyl compound, loss of H₂O, N-alkylation with loss of Cl⁻ to a 2H-pyrrolium ion, proton shift and loss of H⁺ to the aromatic pyrrole. The page gives no conditions.

problems.verificationNote: Viewed: the Named Reactions Explorer page and its two SVG images (general equation and mechanism), downloaded and rendered to PNG. Substitution R¹ = R² = H, R³ = Me chosen here. The Organic Chemistry Portal and TCI sites refused all requests (HTTP 403) during this run, so their pages could not be checked or linked. PubChem (connectivity layer of the InChIKey): ethyl acetoacetate CID 8868, ammonia CID 222, chloroacetaldehyde CID 33 and ethyl 2-methyl-1H-pyrrole-3-carboxylate CID 136747 matched; the enamine intermediate (ethyl 3-aminocrotonate, CID 637551) also matched. Structures a chemist should check: the aldol-type adduct (drawn as the imine, as on the page; the enamine tautomer is accepted), the dehydrated chloro imine, and the regiochemistry of the product (C–C bond to the carbonyl carbon, N–C bond to the CHCl carbon, as drawn on the page). The page's 2H-pyrrolium ions are not asked separately: the comparison key treats the neutral 2H-pyrrole as a tautomer of the product. The page draws the C-attack of the enamine on the carbonyl first (the order of C- and N-alkylation is debated in the literature).

Aldol-type adduct: the enamine α-carbon has added to the aldehyde C=O (imine / enamine tautomers)
Unsaturated chloro imine, after loss of H₂O (the N then displaces Cl⁻ to close the 2H-pyrrolium ring, which loses H⁺ to the pyrrole)
